Container.Name: MeshDash
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted dashboard for Meshtastic mesh radio networks -- packet history, telemetry graphs, an interactive node map, and full messaging, built on 30+ plugins (ISS tracker, weather alerts, task scheduler, and more). GPL-3.0. Docs: https://meshdash.co.uk/docs/
This image is a thin, self-updating runner: on every start it downloads and installs the latest MeshDash release from meshdash.co.uk and needs outbound internet access to do that -- it does not ship a pinned, offline copy of the app.
Runs fully standalone by default, no meshdash.co.uk account needed: open the WebUI and complete the first-run wizard at /setup to connect your radio and create an admin login. Remote access / the optional cloud C2 setup service is opt-in only, off by default -- nothing beyond the version-check/download calls out to meshdash.co.uk unless you fill in the optional MD_SETUP_KEY variable below (see its description).
This template assumes your radio is reached over TCP/Wi-Fi, configured from the /setup wizard -- verified against the runner's source (entrypoint.sh, connections/meshtastic.py) to need no special container privileges, so Privileged stays off and no /dev mapping is added. If you instead connect over USB/Serial, you must add `--privileged` and either `-v /dev:/dev` or a single `--device=/dev/ttyACM0`-style mapping yourself via this template's extra parameters -- neither is enabled here.
Beta: young project (5 commits, no tagged releases as of writing) -- expect breaking changes between updates.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Database (SQLite), logs, plugin data, and the settings file written by the /setup wizard -- persists across the runner's automatic MeshDash version updates. Mounted as a folder, not a file mapping. The image always runs as root with no PUID/PGID support (verified in docker/runner/Dockerfile), so no ownership fix-up is needed or possible.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: MeshDash's web dashboard and /setup wizard. Verified against the runner's entrypoint.sh (28 Sep 2026): defaults to port 8000 unless WEBSERVER_PORT is set. Note: rusjpmd/meshdash-runner's own Docker Hub description claims R3.1+ moved the default to 8181, which contradicts the entrypoint script actually shipped in the current :latest image -- if the WebUI doesn't respond after first boot, check docker logs for the 'Starting MeshDash on port' line and adjust this mapping (and WEBSERVER_PORT below) to match.

Config.Name: WEBSERVER_PORT
Config.Description: Overrides the port MeshDash listens on inside the container -- see the WebUI port note above about the 8000 vs 8181 discrepancy. Change this and the WebUI port mapping together.

Config.Name: MD_SETUP_KEY
Config.Description: Only needed to opt into meshdash.co.uk's cloud C2 setup/remote-management service. Leave blank (default) to run fully standalone with no account -- everything is configured locally via the /setup wizard instead. Setting this alone does nothing: the runner also requires an MD_SETUP_URL variable (deliberately not included in this template) before it will contact meshdash.co.uk for C2 provisioning -- add both yourself via 'Add another Path, Port, Variable...' if you want that feature.
